newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rebel chief threatens to attack Zaire airbase.
newsitem.headline: Rebel chief threatens to attack Zaire airbase.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila threatened on Tuesday to attack Zaire's Kisangani airbase, used to bomb three rebel-held towns in east Zaire on Monday.

"These are terrorist actions. And we are going to get ready to take the war precisely to the place from where the bombers took off," Kabila said in a brief interview broadcast on French LCI television.

Zaire defence officials have said the planes which bombed the towns of Bukavu, Shabunda and Walikale took off from Kisangani where President Mobutu Sese Seko has stationed newly acquired Russian-made jet fighters and helicopter gunships.
Zaire defence officials have reported heavy ground battles around Amisi, 270 km (165 miles) south of Kisangani, the base of the government's faltering mercenary-backed counter-offensive.
The medical charity Medecins sans Frontieres (MSF-Holland) said from Goma that at least nine people were killed and up to 37 wounded in the Bukavu bombing.
A senior Zaire defence official said Goma, the biggest city in rebel hands, was next on the hit list.
The air raids, a marked escalation of the war, appeared designed as a psychological boost for Mobutu's bedraggled army which has lost a vast stretch of borderland to Tutsi-led rebels since October.
By bombing Bukavu, the army symbolically took its much-vaunted counter-offensive to the starting position of the guerrilla campaign close to the Rwanda border.
Zaire's ethnic Tutsis took up arms after local authorities tried to expel them to their ancestral homeland in Rwanda.
